subject: Encoding phased progeny genotypes in F1 fullsib family

messages.author: ff6e05125068c162
messages.subject: Encoding phased progeny genotypes in F1 fullsib family
parts:
I would like to use r/QTL with in an F1 full-sib family descended a cross between to outbred diploid parents.

I have been using OneMap to produce a genetic map from these populations, and am looking to options now to use this map to generate phased genotype probabilities in the progeny (one option that seems to do this is MAPpoly).  Before I go down this road, however, I am hoping to understand better exactly how r/QTL needs to have phased progeny genotypes encoded. 

In particular, it seems like the method to use within r/QTL is to set crosstype = "4-way".  In the documentation for this option, a numeric coding of phased genotypes is described, using as an example a cross between genotypes AB and CD.

For many markers in my dataset, however, there are not 4 distinct alleles (although of course there may be 4 QTL), since I work mostly with biallelic SNPs.  So, for example, I have many markers of the type: AB x AA.  It would seem that progeny with the genotype "BA" could be coded either 2 or 4 according to the numeric re-coding scheme.  

Is this ambiguity irrelevant in this particular case, or is it important that whatever phasing solution I come up be able to explicitly record which homologous chromosome in the parents each progeny genotype came from? 

Hopefully this makes sense & thanks so much for any advice you can provide!
Scott

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Encoding phased progeny genotypes in F1 fullsib family
parts:
Markers segregating like ABxBB (where the female parent is heterozygous) will be about half with the A on one chromosome and half where it's on the other chromosome. Phasing the genotypes identifies those two groups.
Having done that, think of the cross as ABxCD, and the markers as either ABxBB or BAxBB. In each case the progeny are going to be either AB or BB.

ABxBB:
    AB progeny = AC or AD = A = 5
    BB progeny = BC or BD = B = 6

BAxBB: swap the 5's and 6's
    AB progeny = BC or BD = B = 6
    BB progeny = AC or AD = A = 5

If instead the male parent is heterozygous, we'd have

BBxAB:
    AB progeny = AC or BC = C = 7
    BB progeny = AD or BD = D = 8

BBxBA:
    AB progeny = AD or BD = D = 8
    BB progeny = AC or BC = C = 7

karl

messages.author: ff6e05125068c162
messages.subject: Re: Encoding phased progeny genotypes in F1 fullsib family
parts:
Hi Karl,

Thanks very much.  That is indeed what I thought would be the case, and so I remain in need of a phasing solution.

I have not used it, but while looking for solutions to this challenge I found this tool, developed by the group that also wrote OneMap: https://github.com/augusto-garcia/fullsibQTL (described in this pre-print: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2020.12.04.412262v1).

This seems to not only phase progeny genotypes using a linkage map built in OneMap, but also implements interval mapping approaches as well.

Thought you might be interested!

Best,
Scott
